title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 96-98): Grothendieck is building the combinatorics of the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}. He encodes the dual graph of a stable ν-pointed curve X as a 'graphe à bandes aplaties' (m-graph). It has a set Î of half-edges ('bandes') with an involution σ. The fixed points I = Î^σ are the 'flattened bands', i.e. the legs or marked points. The free orbits are the ordinary edges, i.e. the nodes. On the previous page such a graph is shown to be equivalent to an ordinary graph (S, Ã, σ, o) together with a set I and a map I → S. Vertices are drawn as heavy dots and legs as undotted free ends.

This page describes the graph-theoretic effect of partial normalization, i.e. the 'morphismes de normalisation' between m-graphs.

1. The strict case. Take J' ≅ J and I' ≅ I ⊔ J, so the new legs are exactly the half-edges coming from the cut edges. Then G' is obtained from G by choosing a set C of ordinary edges of G. On each edge of C one picks a point and 'cuts' the edge there 'with a snip of the scissors'. Each cut edge thereby becomes two new legs attached to the original endpoints. Geometrically this is passing to the partial normalization of X along the finite set of nodes marked ×. The figure shows a tree-like graph with an edge marked × and a loop marked ×. The second figure shows the result, in which the cut loop gives two new legs at its vertex.

2. Two remarks. The result is again a graph with flattened bands. It may be disconnected even if G was connected. If G had no legs, the result tends to acquire some.

3. The general case. Further remove some of the flattened bands and keep a chosen union of connected components of what remains. The next page notes that components are unchanged by adding or removing legs. This yields the most general relation between G and G' allowed by the definition of normalisation morphisms of m-graphs.

4. Next page. Normalisation morphisms are composed. Strict ones form a category whose isomorphisms are the ordinary isomorphisms and whose morphisms are monomorphisms. Strict sub-objects of G correspond to subsets of the edge set A(G), in parallel with the 'générisation' (edge-contraction) morphisms.

Purpose: to give a combinatorial category indexing boundary strata of the Deligne-Mumford-Knudsen compactification and the clutching/normalisation maps between them. This sits alongside the specialization/generization order on strata.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. In the general (non-strict) case, removing legs may destroy stability of a component; the page does not address stabilization, at least not legibly.

The figures are schematic. The second figure does not obviously show the cut middle edge as two legs, so it may depict a chosen connected component or be drawn loosely. This is a matter of figure clarity rather than a logical error.

ideas.what: Dual graph of a stable pointed curve as a set of half-edges with an involution; fixed points are legs ('bandes aplaties'), free orbits are edges
ideas.modern_name: Stable graph / modular graph in half-edge (flag) formalism
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kontsevich; Getzler-Kapranov (1998); Manin; Behrend; also implicit in Knudsen/Deligne-Mumford
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses the stratification of \bar M_{g,ν} and dual graphs only informally

ideas.what: Partial normalization along a set C of nodes equals cutting the edges of C, each giving two new legs; the result may be disconnected
ideas.modern_name: Cutting/ungrafting of edges; inverse of clutching morphisms ξ_Γ
ideas.usually_credited_to: Knudsen (1983, clutching maps); standard in Arbarello-Cornalba, Getzler-Kapranov

ideas.what: Normalisation morphisms of m-graphs (cut edges, delete legs, select components) forming a category; strict ones are monomorphisms with subobjects equal to subsets of edges, parallel to generization (contraction) morphisms
ideas.modern_name: Graph categories with cutting/contraction morphisms (Borisov-Manin graph category; Joyal-Kock; categories indexing modular operads)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, apparently in the early 1980s, a category of 'm-graphs' with two kinds of morphisms. 'Normalisation' morphisms cut edges into legs, forget legs and choose connected components; 'générisation' morphisms contract edges. He analyses subobject lattices as power sets of edge sets. This anticipates the graph categories later used to define modular operads and the Borisov-Manin category of graphs, which includes both cutting and contraction. Such constructions are not credited to him.
missed.quote: en "coupant" l'arête en ce point avec un coup de ciseaux ... On trouve un nouveau graphe à bandes aplaties (qui a des chances d'être disconnexe, même si G était connexe)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical priority only. The mathematics itself (clutching/normalisation of stable curves) is standard Knudsen/Deligne-Mumford material. The categorical packaging is mildly anticipatory but well developed in the later literature.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard description of how dual graphs change under partial normalization. The only notable aspect is the early categorical organisation, which prefigures Getzler-Kapranov and Borisov-Manin graph categories.
transcription_corrections: 'avec un cap de ...[?]' should read 'avec un coup de ciseaux' (a snip of the scissors).

'prenant le diagramme de X suivant la partie finie marquée ×' more likely reads 'prenant le normalisé (partiel) de X suivant la partie finie marquée ×'. This is uncertain, but the sense is partial normalization at the marked nodes.
Top-left margin: 'cas d'une compactification[?] stricte' is more plausibly 'cas d'une normalisation stricte', matching 'morphismes de normalisation stricts' on the next page.
'on obtient G' à partir de G*' : G* is probably just G.
'si G n'avait pas de bandes aplaties, il a tendance : en ...' probably reads 'il a tendance à en avoir' (it tends to acquire some).
